summary: Preserved candidate PR 1122's xgrammar pattern/length admission guard and corrected its remaining object-level allOf blind spot, including local $defs references. Both counterexamples from review PR 1182 were reproduced at exact candidate commit 1b5d79c0a1c7553c3bcfac31ca07dd614897564c before the correction.

tests.what_was_measured: Both reviewed schemas had detected=False and admission_rejected=False, while raw xgrammar accepted the minLength-violating document. See evidence/review-counterexamples-before.log.
Both reviewed schemas are now detected and rejected at admission; raw xgrammar 0.2.1 remains independently confirmed to accept the invalid document.
42 tests passed with 34 subtests, covering direct and composed rejection plus boundaries for anyOf and different property locations.
Repository formatting and static checks for the changed source and regression test.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are deterministic CPU-only JSON-schema admission/compiler behavior; no model or GPU execution was used.

remaining_limitations: This guard targets xgrammar 0.2.x's demonstrated lossy pattern plus minLength/maxLength behavior; it does not claim to repair xgrammar itself.
No HTTP serving or model-weight validation was performed because neither is needed to exercise admission and raw grammar compilation.
